g1|core|third-party|standard third-party.title: Third-Party Order Processing with Automatic Purchase Requisition (TAS)
g1|core|third-party|standard third-party.story: When a customer buys something we do not stock, our system automatically tells an external vendor to ship the item directly to them and send us the bill. In SAP S/4HANA Order-to-Cash (OTC), this process creates a sales order with item category TAS, which immediately generates a purchase requisition in Materials Management (MM) to trigger the third-party vendor fulfillment.
g1|core|third-party|standard third-party.why_business_needs_it: This process allows companies to expand their product catalog and fulfill customer demands without holding physical inventory or incurring warehousing costs. It automates vendor procurement directly from sales order entry, reducing manual processing time and order-to-delivery cycles.

modules.role: Captures customer demand via sales order OR, assigns item category TAS, triggers procurement, and bills the customer based on incoming vendor invoices.
modules.hands_off_to: MM (Materials Management) to create and process the automatic purchase requisition and subsequent purchase order.

modules.role: Receives the purchase requisition from the sales order, generates the purchase order to the external vendor, and processes the vendor invoice receipt.
modules.hands_off_to: FI (Financial Accounting) for vendor liability posting and customer billing generation.

modules.role: Posts vendor invoice liabilities and issues customer invoices based on order-related billing control.

g1|core|third-party|third-party with man.title: Third-Party Order Processing with Manual Purchase Requisition (TAT)
g1|core|third-party|third-party with man.story: Imagine a store selling a giant bicycle that they do not have in their warehouse, so they ask another factory to ship it straight to the customer's doorstep while the store handles the bill. More precisely, in SAP S/4HANA Order-to-Cash (OTC), Third-Party Order Processing with a manual purchase requisition (TAT) triggers a procurement hand-off from a sales order item where a buyer manually creates a purchase requisition instead of the system doing it automatically.
g1|core|third-party|third-party with man.why_business_needs_it: This process allows companies to fulfill customer demand for specialized or out-of-stock items using external vendors without holding physical inventory, while retaining full control over manual procurement review and customer billing. It bridges the sales order directly to procurement and subsequently enables order-related billing upon vendor delivery.

modules.role: Captures customer demand via sales order OR with item category TAT, passes requirements to MM, and generates order-related customer billing upon fulfillment.
modules.hands_off_to: MM (Materials Management) via manual purchase requisition creation.

modules.role: Manages vendor master data, purchasing info records, and manual purchase requisition conversion into purchase orders sent to the external vendor.
modules.hands_off_to: FI (Financial Accounting) for vendor invoice verification and customer billing.

modules.role: Posts customer invoices resulting from billing and vendor liabilities resulting from goods receipts or vendor invoice verification.

g1|core|third-party|third-party with cus.title: Third-Party Order Processing with Customer Returns
g1|core|third-party|third-party with cus.story: Imagine a customer buys a special toy from our shop, but instead of us sending it from our shelf, our friend the vendor ships it straight to their house. When the customer decides to return that toy, our vendor takes it back directly and gives us a credit note so we can refund the customer. Technically, this process handles customer returns for third-party business transactions using sales document type RE, item category REN, schedule line category RN, and a returns purchase requisition that triggers vendor credit processing upon goods receipt.
g1|core|third-party|third-party with cus.why_business_needs_it: It allows companies to handle customer returns for direct-delivery items without physically receiving the stock into their own warehouse. This ensures accurate vendor credit memo processing and smooth financial settlements with both the customer and the external supplier.

g1|panel|third-party.otc_impact: Third-party order processing sits at the intersection of Order-to-Cash and MM-PUR, shifting the execution model by routing customer demand directly to an external vendor who ships straight to the customer. For OTC, this changes the document flow: sales orders create a purchase requisition automatically or manually, bypassing internal outbound deliveries and goods issues, while customer billing is triggered either upon incoming vendor invoice verification or immediately upon order entry. This integration requires precise schedule line category configuration to ensure correct pricing, tax determination, and revenue recognition without generating physical warehouse stock movements.

panel_qa.question: How do we choose between automatic purchase requisition creation (TAS) and manual purchase requisition creation (TAT) in our sales document schedule line categories?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: The business scenario involves balancing automated fulfillment velocity against commercial control for specialized third-party items. SAP is configured this way to let standard item category determination drive the schedule line category (e.g., CS for standard third-party), which links to item category attribute TAS for automatic purchase requisition generation in MM, or TAT where a buyer must manually review and release the requisition in transaction ME51N/ME54N. The key configuration is maintaining table T163K and setting the item category usage in Customizing under Sales and Distribution > Sales Documents > Schedule Lines > Define Schedule Line Categories. The leadership value is that TAS eliminates procurement touchpoints for high-volume catalog items, reducing administrative overhead and order cycle time, whereas TAT protects profit margins on high-value engineered goods by enforcing commercial review before commitment. Next, we will audit our material master classification to ensure all third-party items point to the correct item category group. The weak answer is to say we use automatic for everything because it is faster, ignoring the risk of unverified vendor costs.
panel_qa.trap: We just use automatic for everything because it is faster.

panel_qa.question: What is the financial and operational impact on OTC when a third-party vendor invoices us for a quantity different from what we confirmed to the customer?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: The business scenario addresses quantity and price variances that occur between customer order commitments and vendor settlement in third-party drop shipments. SAP is configured this way to support order-related billing (Billing Type F2) tied to either the incoming vendor invoice via Evaluated Receipt Settlement (ERS) or standard Logistics Invoice Verification (MIRO), rather than a physical Goods Issue. The key configuration involves setting the billing relevance indicator 'F' (Order-rel. billing spec.qty/der.from inv.rec.) in Customizing for Sales and Distribution > Billing > Billing Documents > Define Billing Relevance. The leadership value is protecting gross margin integrity by ensuring we bill the customer accurately based on verified procurement costs, thereby mitigating leakage and audit compliance risks. Next, we are implementing automated tolerance checks in MIRO to catch discrepancies before billing generation. The weak answer is that billing just copies the sales order quantity regardless of what the vendor actually billed.
panel_qa.trap: Billing just copies the sales order quantity regardless of what the vendor actually billed.

panel_qa.question: How does our SAP S/4HANA architecture handle customer returns against a third-party sales order without triggering an internal warehouse physical receipt?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: The business scenario covers the reverse logistics flow when a end-customer rejects or returns goods delivered directly by a third-party vendor. SAP is configured this way using Return Order type RE with item category REN, where schedule line category determines that no inventory movement occurs in our plant, but instead triggers a return purchase order or credit memo workflow to the vendor. The key configuration requires mapping the returns item category in SD Customizing under Sales and Distribution > Sales Documents > Sales Document Item > Assign Item Categories, linked to a returns schedule line that does not trigger delivery requirements. The leadership value is maintaining accurate financial accounting by issuing credit memos only after vendor credit confirmation, preventing phantom inventory discrepancies and write-offs in our warehouse management systems. Next, we will configure output types for automated return notification transmittal to vendors via EDI 860. The weak answer is that we create a standard return delivery to the main warehouse, ignoring the fact that the goods came from an external vendor.
panel_qa.trap: We create a standard return delivery to the main warehouse.

panel_qa.question: How do we prevent revenue leakage when sales orders are stuck in third-party processing because the purchase requisition has not been converted to a purchase order?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: The business scenario focuses on pipeline visibility and order bottlenecks where sales orders remain open indefinitely because procurement has not acted on the generated purchase requisition. SAP is configured this way to maintain a strict linkage between the SD sales document flow (table VBFA) and the MM purchasing document tables (EBKN, EKKO), pausing billing until procurement completion depending on billing relevance settings. The key configuration is utilizing standard SAP Fiori app 'Monitor External Procurement' (App ID F1995) to track unconverted purchase requisitions originating from sales orders. The leadership value is accelerating cash velocity and improving working capital metrics by reducing order-to-invoice cycle time for drop-shipped revenue. Next, we are deploying automated workflow alerts for buyers when third-party requisitions age past 48 hours. The weak answer is to wait for the customer to call complaining that their invoice or shipment never arrived.
panel_qa.trap: We wait for the customer to call complaining that their invoice or shipment never arrived.

panel_qa.question: What pricing and tax determination challenges arise when a third-party vendor ships from a location in a different state or country than our sales organization's plant?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: The business scenario deals with multi-jurisdictional tax implications and cost-plus pricing structures in direct drop-ship transactions. SAP is configured this way by utilizing the delivering plant assigned in the sales order item or purchase requisition to determine the tax classification and jurisdiction code, while fetching vendor-specific purchase prices via condition records (PB00) into the sales order condition screen. The key configuration involves maintaining condition technique in pricing procedure RVAA01 with access sequences pointing to vendor-material info records (ME11). The leadership value is ensuring statutory tax compliance and preventing margin erosion by automatically factoring freight and localized tax rules into customer quotations. Next, we are integrating tax engines like Vertex via Tax Interface to automate complex cross-border drop-ship tax determination. The weak answer is that system pricing just pulls the standard material master price without checking vendor agreements.
panel_qa.trap: System pricing just pulls the standard material master price without checking vendor agreements.

panel_qa.question: How do we ensure that credit management blocks correctly apply to third-party orders before the purchase requisition is transmitted to the vendor?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: The business scenario involves credit risk mitigation, ensuring that financially delinquent customers cannot commit our company to external vendor purchase liabilities. SAP is configured this way using SAP Credit Management (FSCM / UKM) integrated with sales order creation, where a credit check failure places a delivery and billing block on the sales order, which in turn prevents the automatic creation or release of the purchase requisition in MM. The key configuration is assigning credit check rules in Financial Supply Chain Management > Credit Management > Credit Risk Monitoring > Define Credit Limit Check, combined with SD schedule line blocking indicators. The leadership value is safeguarding the balance sheet against bad debt by stopping procurement commitments for high-risk accounts before cash is exposed. Next, we will review our credit segment assignments to ensure third-party orders are included in total exposure calculations. The weak answer is that purchase requisitions are created immediately upon order save regardless of customer credit status.

errors.title: Vendor Invoice Blocked Due to Goods Receipt Flag
errors.plain_meaning: The system is waiting for a warehouse receiving dock scan that will never happen because the goods went directly to the customer. Transaction MIRO stops vendor invoice posting because the purchase order line item has the Goods Receipt-Based Invoice Verification flag enabled, preventing customer invoice release in OTC.
errors.cause: The purchase order line item created for third-party item category S has the 'GR-based IV' checkbox (field EKPO-WEBRE) activated. Because the standard TAS flow does not involve physical warehouse goods receipt (MIGO), MIRO requires a goods receipt posting before invoice entry, which stops the downstream customer billing document from ever being generated.
errors.config_step: Define Purchasing Info Record (ME11) / Vendor Master Purchasing Data (BP)
errors.verify: Re-run transaction MIRO for the purchase order; the line item successfully populates the invoice verification grid without generating error M8 081.
errors.prevent: Configure purchasing info record categories for third-party items to default without the GR-based invoice verification flag.

fix_steps.step: Inspect purchase order line item invoice controls
fix_steps.values: De-select the 'GR-based IV' checkbox (EKPO-WEBRE); ensure field 'Inv. receipt' (EKPO-REPOS) remains checked.

fix_steps.values: Enter Vendor, Material, Purchasing Org, Plant; select 'Purchasing Org. Data 1'; uncheck 'GR-Based IV' (EINE-WEBRE).

errors.title: Cost Missing on Sales Order Third-Party Line
errors.where_seen: VA01 / VA02 -- Sales Order Processing (Conditions Tab)
errors.plain_meaning: The system cannot calculate how much profit is made on the sale because it does not know what the supplier charges. In sales order item pricing, condition type VPRS fails to obtain a cost value because no purchasing info record, vendor contract, or valuation condition exists for the third-party material.
errors.cause: Pricing condition type VPRS has condition category 'G' (Cost). For third-party item category TAS, the sales order cost must be determined from a valid Purchasing Info Record or vendor purchasing condition; if no valid purchasing price is found and the material master lacks a standard or moving average valuation price, condition VPRS remains zero, triggering an incomplete pricing status.
errors.config_step: Maintain Purchasing Info Record (ME11) & Condition Type VPRS Control (V/06)
errors.verify: Open the sales order in VA03, navigate to the Item Conditions tab, and verify condition VPRS displays an active, positive valuation rate matching the purchasing info record.
errors.prevent: Mandate purchasing info record creation or vendor source list maintenance as a required master data prerequisite before releasing new third-party trading goods in sales org catalogs.

errors.title: Automatic Purchase Requisition Generation Fails on Account Assignment
errors.where_seen: VA01 -- Saving Sales Order (Schedule Line CS Processing)
errors.plain_meaning: The sales order cannot automatically order goods from the supplier because the accounting bookkeeping account is missing. When schedule line category CS attempts to generate a purchase requisition upon sales order save, account determination fails to supply a general ledger consumption account for account assignment category X.
errors.cause: Schedule line category CS creates a Purchase Requisition using Account Assignment Category X (Third-party) and Item Category S. Table T030 (Automatic Account Determination) lacks a configuration entry under transaction key GBB with general account modifier VAX for the valuation grouping code and valuation class assigned to the material, causing PR creation to abort.
errors.config_step: Configure Account Assignment Category X (OME9) & Configure Automatic Postings (OBYC)
errors.verify: Re-enter transaction VA01 to create the OR sales order with TAS item and CS schedule line; save the order and confirm a Purchase Requisition number is populated in VBBE/VBEP table without prompting for manual account entry.
errors.prevent: Implement a financial account determination checklist requiring transaction key GBB / VAX and VBR mapping across all company charts of accounts during plant and material type onboarding.

fix_steps.values: Select Category 'X'; verify Account Modification is 'VAX', Consumption Posting is 'V', and Valuation Path indicator is maintained.

fix_steps.values: Record field BKLAS (Valuation Class) for the material in the delivering plant.

fix_steps.step: Maintain automatic G/L account assignment
fix_steps.values: Enter Chart of Accounts; add table row: Valuation Modification (grouping code), General Modification 'VAX', Valuation Class from MM03, and debit/credit G/L Consumption Account (COGS Third-Party).

errors.title: Incompatible Schedule Line Category for Third-Party Item
errors.where_seen: VA01 / VA02 -- Sales Order Schedule Line Tab
errors.message_text: Item category &1 cannot be used with schedule line &2
errors.plain_meaning: The sales order cannot link the customer line item to the supplier purchasing schedule because the connection rule is missing. Transaction VA01 halts because item category TAS is not configured to accept schedule line category CS in sales customizing table TVEPZ.
errors.cause: Customizing table TVEPZ (Schedule Line Category Determination) lacks an entry mapping sales document item category TAS and MRP type (or blank MRP type) to default schedule line category CS, or a user manually entered an unsupported schedule line category (such as CP or CN) against item category TAS.
errors.verify: Create a new sales order in VA01 using document type OR and material with item category group BANC; verify that line item category TAS resolves to schedule line category CS automatically.
errors.prevent: Lock table TVEPZ transports to authorized OTC leads to avoid accidental deletion of schedule line category mappings during release upgrades.

fix_steps.where: SPRO -> Sales and Distribution -> Sales -> Sales Documents -> Schedule Lines -> Assign Schedule Line Categories (VOV5)
fix_steps.values: Locate or create table entry: Item Category: TAS, MRP Type: blank (or specific MRP type like ND), Default Schedule Line Category: CS.

fix_steps.values: Ensure manual schedule line alternatives (such as manual third-party or inquiry categories) are added under 'Manual schedule line category' columns if needed.

fix_steps.values: Open sales order item schedule lines tab; confirm schedule line category defaults to 'CS' automatically based on item category TAS.

errors.title: Purchase Order Blocked Missing Ship-To Address
errors.where_seen: ME21N / ME59N -- Purchase Order Creation from PR
errors.message_text: Third-party item requires customer delivery address
errors.plain_meaning: The supplier does not know where to deliver the goods because the customer's shipping address is missing from the purchase order. Converting the sales-order-generated purchase requisition into a purchase order via ME21N or ME59N fails because account assignment category X requires a valid ship-to customer address record.
errors.cause: The purchase requisition created by schedule line category CS carries the customer number (KUNNR) from the sales order ship-to partner (WE). If the customer business partner address master data in table ADRC has missing mandatory fields (such as postal code, street, or country key), or if field EKPO-KUNNR was cleared during manual PR processing, ME21N/ME59N blocks PO creation.
errors.config_step: Define Account Assignment Categories (OME9) & Business Partner Address Data (BP)
errors.verify: Convert the PR to a PO using transaction ME21N or batch job ME59N; verify the system saves the purchase order document without message 06 248.
errors.prevent: Set address fields as required attributes in Business Partner customer account group configurations to prevent creation of incomplete ship-to party accounts.
